programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: A lace bra and knicker set tests the sewers before they turn thermals into daywear. They must then fit a pair of luxury pyjamas to their male models. One sewers wins Garment of the Week, and another is asked to leave the Sewing Room

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The quarter finalists go back to the 1930s to take women’s sailor trousers. They also turn men’s shirts into 1930s women’s blouses and fit glamorous bias-cut evening gowns reminiscent of outfits worn by Katherine Hepburn and Bette Davis.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Sara Pascoe welcomes the four semi-finalists into the Sewing Room to celebrate the influences of Japanese design and sewing. The Sewers follow the patterns for a kimono inspired dress, mend old denim using Japanese techniques and create an outfit using folding and pleating

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the final, and the sewers take on a trio of party themed challenges. They start with the pattern for Esme’s iconic Amorphous dress, use old scraps to make a party outfit and fit red-carpet-worthy jumpsuits. The judges have the difficult task of deciding who will be crowed by Britain’s best sewer

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Sara Pascoe welcomes 12 new sewers to the Sewing Bee. Judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young test the sewers with ‘Classics with a Twist’. The sewers make a top with a twist, transform the office uniform into a new look to reflect their style and create a dress that has cut out details to fit their models.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s not exactly a holiday for the sewers, as judges Patrick and Esme task them with creating garments based around a travel wardrobe. They’re asked to create a rucksack and a swimsuit and to transform windbreakers. Who will make a splash, and who will take a nose dive and leave the competition?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate clothes from west Africa. Guest judge Nigerian fashion designer Banke Kuku joins Esme and Patrick this week. Who will impress all three judges and win Garment of the Week, and who will become the third sewer to leave the competition?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Taking on the fashion industry, the second most polluting industry in the world, it’s Reduce, Reuse and Recycle week. The sewers attempt a zero waste pattern for a pair of trousers, transform several bags in to a garment and source second hand crochet blankets to create new outfits.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s Art week as the remaining sewers tackle three challenges inspired by the world of art. The sewers make a skirt inspired by the modernist movement, transform canvases into dresses, and draw on artists’ dreams to create fantastical outfits for a mind bending catwalk.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s Kids week in the sewing room, and Sara Pascoe invites the seven remaining sewers to make a child’s dragon dressing gown. In the transformation challenge, the sewers personalise denim jackets using hand-me-downs. Finally mini models have fancy dress outfits created ready for the party.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Its week 7 and we’re going back to the 90s with cargo pants, 90s icon fancy dress and body skimming supermodel dresses. Who will make it into the quarter final, and who will take a tumble on the catwalk and leave the sewing room?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 8, and the remaining sewers celebrate fashion icons with little black dresses, a shower curtain transformation and smoking jackets. Who will secure icon status and win Garment of the Week, and who will be a fashion fail?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the semi-final, and this week it’s three utilitarian clothing; the trench coat, housework garments and boiler suits.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the final of The Great British Sewing Bee, and the sewers face three challenges including a Victoriana dress, fabulous men’s outfits and a two-in-one dress. Past contestants return for a reunion, while the judges decide who will be crowned this year’s best amateur sewer.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Kiell Smith-Bynoe welcomes the 12 sewers as we kick off the tenth series. Judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young set the challenges. The Pattern challenge is a denim A-line midiskirt, they’re asked to transform t-shirts and the made to measure is to create a casual day dress to fit their models.

programme.title: Baking Show The Professionals
programme.desc: The six teams tackle two miniature classics, strawberry tarts and fruit salad, before reinventing the retro pineapple upside-down cake. As always, they face two days of testing challenges judged by two world class patisserie experts, Benoit Blin and Cherish Finden

programme.title: Baking Show The Professionals
programme.desc: The five remaining teams make the classic layered dessert millefeuille, master the art of illusion, and create a bird-themed pièce montée adorned with Paris-Brest. The pressure and the difficulty of the challenges is ramping up with every week that the teams stay in the competition.

programme.title: Baking Show The Professionals
programme.desc: This week the judges have a surprise up their sleeves with a challenge never before seen on Baking ShowThe Professionals in the shape of a secret challenge for the teams. Which of the teams will rise to the challenge and which will fall at this first chocolate challenge?

programme.title: Baking Show The Professionals
programme.desc: Six new teams make tarte chiboust vallée d'Auge and rice puddings, before reinventing the Key lime pie, complete with breathtaking towering edible sculptures, for their showpiece. Judging their efforts are world class Patissier Chefs Benoit Blin and Cherish Finden.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s sports week in the sewing room. In the first challenge, the sewers are presented with a pattern for a half zip fleece, then transform a whole new outfit from cricket whites and protection. Finally, the sewers make an outfit for a specific sport fit for an international event.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 3 of the Sewing Bee, and the sewers face three challenges inspired by travel. They are asked to create summer blouses from tablecloths, nautical bags and French Riviera outfits. Who will make a fashion faux pas and who will turn heads with some je ne sais quoi?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Kiell Smith-Bynoe welcomes back Reduce Reuse Recycle week. First, the sewers attempt a quilted bag using scraps. In the transformation challenge the sewers use textile waste to create a new item. Finally, the sewers take wedding dressed and repurpose them into an outfit for a party.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: Kiell Smith-Bynoe and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, Priya Khanchandani. This week the sewers celebrate fashion and textile from India. They create Nehru jackets, transform calico and Madras fabrics into an outift, and create garments inspired by saris.
